original_question: Given a signed graph Γ = (G, σ), define a complement signed graph Γ̄ = (Ḡ, σ̄) whose underlying graph is the usual graph complement and for which useful spectral relations with the complete signed graph Γ ∪ Γ̄ hold.
target_in_paper: Problem 3.29 in Section 3.7 asks for a definition of the complement Γ̄=(Ḡ,σ̄) of a signed graph Γ=(G,σ), with Ḡ the usual complement of G, so that nice spectral properties arise from the complete signed graph Γ∪Γ̄. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's core content: it starts from a signed graph Γ=(G,σ), requires the underlying graph of the complement to be the ordinary graph complement Ḡ, and asks for spectral behavior to be tied to the complete signed graph Γ∪Γ̄. This is essentially Problem 3.29. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
missing_details: The paper states this as an open problem for arbitrary signed graphs, so the universal quantifier should be explicit: for every signed graph Γ=(G,σ). ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

Γ̄ is implicitly on the same vertex set as Γ, with underlying graph Ḡ, so that Γ∪Γ̄ is a complete signed graph. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

The paper intentionally leaves the desired conclusion open-ended: the goal is to choose σ̄ so that nice spectral properties can be derived from Γ∪Γ̄, not to impose one specific spectral formula. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

The ambient spectral convention comes from the introduction: throughout the paper, spectrum is primarily the adjacency spectrum of the signed adjacency matrix A(Γ), a real symmetric {0,±1}-matrix. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

No extra assumptions such as connectivity, balance, regularity, or switching stability are part of Problem 3.29, so they should not be added in a paper-faithful restatement. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))

There are no relevant algebraic side conditions here such as field choice, homogeneity, degree bounds, or nilpotency; the only implicit operator that needs naming is the signed adjacency matrix/spectrum. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
refined_question: In the adjacency-spectral setting of the paper, for every signed graph Γ=(G,σ), can one define a signed complement Γ̄=(Ḡ,σ̄) on the same vertex set, where Ḡ is the ordinary graph complement of G, such that nice spectral properties can be derived from the complete signed graph Γ∪Γ̄? ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
justification: This is the nearest official formulation because Section 3.7 first explains that signed graph theory still lacks a satisfactory notion of complement, then immediately poses Problem 3.29 in almost the same form as your draft. The surrounding context shows that the task is to define the signature on the complement itself, not to broaden the question to a larger theory, and the introduction fixes the paper's default spectral meaning as adjacency spectrum. I therefore kept the question narrow and did not add switching, balance, or regularity requirements that the paper does not state. ([sites.udel.edu](https://sites.udel.edu/cioaba/files/2019/07/SignedGraphsSurveyJuly09.pdf))
